questions.question: What is the basic purpose of physics support in a virtual world generator?
options: To make the virtual world align with a user's matched zone.
To make locomotion replace the basic laws of mechanics.
To make real-world events have similar virtual-world events.
To make rendering depend only on computer vision techniques.
questions.explanation: Physics support is meant to make the virtual world appear to behave like the real world.

questions.question: How should a virtual world generator usually treat object motion?
options: With rendering support only, because graphics can determine motion.
With matched-motion tracking data alone, without physical laws.
With basic laws of mechanics, adding advanced laws when more realism is desirable.
With advanced laws of mechanics only, because basic laws are insufficient.
questions.explanation: Support for basic mechanical laws should be good enough, and advanced laws may be added for extra realism.

questions.question: What should physics support do to a dropped ball in a virtual world?
options: Move it at a constant speed toward the ground.
Keep it still until another body causes a collision.
Rotate it to match the user's rotational movement.
Make it accelerate toward the ground due to gravity.
questions.explanation: A dropped ball should not be moved at constant speed; gravity should make it accelerate toward the ground.

questions.question: Which two capabilities should ideally be included in collision support?
options: Collision detection and collision response.
Graphics support and computer vision support
Rendering support and collaborative VR support
Locomotion support and matched motion support
questions.explanation: Collision detection determines whether bodies intersect, and collision response determines their behavior after a collision.

questions.question: Besides object motion and collisions, what should physics support replicate?
options: Light propagation, surface interaction, illumination, sound, and smell.
Triangular meshes, rendering, and panoramic video
Matched zones, facial expressions, and body language
SLAM positioning, translational movement, and rotational movement
questions.explanation: Physics support should also replicate phenomena such as how light propagates and interacts with surfaces, illumination effects, and how sound and smell propagate.

questions.question: In a networked collaborative virtual reality experience, what is maintained by a system or a server?
options: Each user's matched zone
A headset's tracking data
The physical real-world space
The shared virtual world
questions.explanation: A networked collaborative VR experience maintains a shared virtual world by a system or server, although a network experience may not be required everywhere.

questions.question: What is usually true about matched zones in a networked collaborative virtual reality setting?
options: They are mostly disjoint and distributed around the Earth.
They always overlap in the real world.
They remove the need to avoid physical collision when users are close.
They are identical for every user.
questions.explanation: Matched zones may overlap in the real world, but most often they are disjoint and distributed around the Earth, so physical collision must still be avoided when users are close.

questions.question: Whether users are close or spread around the world, what must manage user interactions, including collisions, in the shared virtual world?
options: A server only when users are far apart
The users' physical surroundings
The matched zones themselves
The virtual reality system
questions.explanation: User interactions, including collisions, must be managed by the virtual reality system regardless of whether users are close or spread around the world.

questions.question: What should a virtual world generator support when social interaction is important in a networked collaborative virtual reality setting?
options: Tracking data and graphical rendering calls
Collision detection and collision response
Eye movements, facial expressions, and body language
Gravity, lighting, and sound propagation
questions.explanation: When social interaction is important, the virtual world generator should support eye movements, facial expressions, and body language, and matched motion burden may increase as users meet.

questions.question: Compared with using a ready-made virtual world generator, what is a key advantage of building a virtual world generator from a basic software development kit?
options: It provides built-in collision and physics support out of the box.
It gives maximum control and performance optimization by letting the developer choose physics algorithms.
It requires the developer to use fixed algorithms supplied by a package.
It avoids the need to implement physics support from scratch.
questions.explanation: Building from a basic SDK lets the developer choose and implement physics support algorithms according to performance, giving maximum control and optimization.

questions.question: When a developer builds a virtual world generator from a basic software development kit, what must they build at the very least?
options: The tracking APIs that access tracking data.
The menu options used to customize a ready-made virtual world generator.
The basic drivers that drive the headset or device hardware.
The physics support, including avatar movement, collision detection and response, lighting models, and audio support.
questions.explanation: A developer building a virtual world generator from a basic SDK must build at least the physics support of the virtual world, handling avatar movement, collisions, lighting, and audio.

questions.question: How does a ready-made virtual world generator both help and limit a developer creating a virtual reality experience?
options: It increases effort by requiring the developer to build all physics support from scratch, but it gives full algorithmic control.
It provides only low-level drivers and tracking APIs, so the developer must write all high-level scripts.
It is best for highly original experiences because it avoids any preexisting function supports or algorithms.
It reduces effort by including collision and physics support, but its own function supports and algorithms can restrict highly original experiences.
questions.explanation: A ready-made virtual world generator makes creation easier by providing supports such as collisions or physics, but the developer must use its existing supports and algorithm implementations, which can restrict highly original experiences.

questions.question: What is a basic software development kit for a headset, device, or platform typically expected to provide?
options: Basic drivers, APIs for accessing tracking data, and APIs for calling graphical rendering libraries.
Menu options and high-level scripts for customizing a ready-made virtual world generator.
Complete support for locomotion, matched motion, physics, and networked collaborative virtual reality.
A shared virtual world maintained by a server for all connected users.
questions.explanation: A basic SDK typically provides drivers, tracking-data APIs, and rendering-library APIs, but it does not normally take care of every aspect of locomotion, matched motion, physics, or networked collaborative virtual reality.

questions.question: A virtual reality game engine is best described as which kind of software?
options: A rendering API that sits between hardware and higher-level application software
A basic SDK that sits between hardware and higher-level application software
Middleware that sits between hardware and higher-level application software
A virtual world generator that sits between hardware and higher-level application software
questions.explanation: A VR engine or game engine is middleware that sits between hardware and higher-level application software and abstracts hardware functionalities for XR application developers.

questions.question: Which set of items can be components of a game engine?
options: A physics engine, a rendering engine, a GPU driver, and a user interface
A physics engine, a rendering engine, a headset sensor, and a user interface
A physics engine, a rendering engine, an input device, and a user interface
A physics engine, a rendering engine, an audio engine, and a user interface
questions.explanation: A game engine can be thought of schematically as comprising components such as a physics engine, a rendering engine, an audio engine, and a user interface.

questions.question: What three kinds of options may an authoring tool for a game engine provide?
options: Driver options, feature-setting options, and logic-setting options
Loading options, feature-setting options, and hardware options
Loading options, driver options, and logic-setting options
Loading options, feature-setting options, and logic-setting options
questions.explanation: An authoring tool may provide loading options, feature-setting options, and logic-setting options, with logic setting sometimes done through scripting.

questions.question: In a typical game engine, which core support is primarily for multiplayer collaborative virtual reality experiences?
options: Physics support
Rendering support
Audio support
Networking support
questions.explanation: Typical game engine core functionalities include networking support primarily for multiplayer collaborative VR experiences.

questions.question: What is the main role of a rendering engine inside a game engine?
options: Generating animated 3D graphics through methods such as rasterization or ray tracing
Emulating physical forces and collisions acting on scene objects
Providing software abstractions of the central processing unit
Loading, modifying, and generating sound through a speaker system
questions.explanation: A rendering engine helps generate animated three-dimensional graphics using rendering methods such as rasterization or ray tracing.

questions.question: Rendering APIs such as Direct3D, OpenGL, and Vulkan provide a rendering engine with what?
options: Software abstractions of the central processing unit
Software abstractions of a speaker system
Software abstractions of the graphics processing unit
Software abstractions of system memory
questions.explanation: A rendering engine is typically built on rendering APIs that provide software abstractions of the GPU.

questions.question: Why is an audio engine not typically associated with a GPU?
options: It uses the GPU because audio APIs are built on graphics hardware
It can run on a CPU or ASIC, and GPUs are generally associated with graphics or rendering
It requires the GPU to modify and generate sound in real time
It depends on the GPU to synchronize sound with three-dimensional motion
questions.explanation: An audio engine can perform its calculations on a CPU or a dedicated ASIC and does not require a GPU, while GPUs are generally associated with graphics or rendering.

questions.question: Which game-engine component simulates physical forces and collisions acting on objects at runtime?
options: The audio engine
A rendering API
The physics engine
The rendering engine
questions.explanation: The physics engine provides functions for simulating physical forces and collisions acting on various objects in a scene at runtime.

questions.question: How do Unreal Engine and Unity 3D differ in terms of availability and licensing?
options: Unity 3D's major features are freely available, whereas Unreal Engine is proprietary with a limited free version
Unreal Engine's major features are freely available, whereas Unity 3D is proprietary with a limited free version
Both engines are fully proprietary and do not offer any free versions
Both engines are fully open source and available without licensing restrictions
questions.explanation: Unreal Engine's major features are freely available, while Unity 3D is proprietary, has a free version with limitations, and offers more flexibility in its proprietary versions.

questions.question: How does web application deployment for a VR experience differ from native application deployment?
options: Native deployment can be used remotely without a specific device, whereas web deployment requires platform-specific SDKs.
Native deployment is categorized only by whether the SDK is for VR or AR applications.
Web deployment is an installable package of tools for designing, building, and testing VR experiences.
Web deployment can be used remotely without a specific device, whereas native deployment requires platform-specific SDKs.
questions.explanation: Web application deployment allows the experience to be obtained remotely without a specific device, while native deployment requires SDKs tailored to the platform and hardware.

questions.question: What is a VR software development kit?
options: A game-engine component that simulates physical forces and collisions at runtime.
An installable collection of tools for a specific hardware and operating system combination to design, build, and test VR experiences.
A hardware component that speeds up the rendering of animated 3D graphics.
A rendering API that provides a software abstraction of a graphics processing unit.
questions.explanation: An SDK is a collection of software development tools in one installable package specific to a hardware and operating system combination, providing tools to design, build, and test VR experiences.

questions.question: In VR deployment, what does the term platform usually mean?
options: The rendering APIs used by a rendering engine.
The application software above the game engine.
The head-mounted display that presents the virtual environment.
The operating system together with the hardware.
questions.explanation: In deployment, a platform typically means the operating system plus the hardware, such as Windows or Mac OS for desktop platforms and Android or iOS for mobile platforms.

questions.question: Native VR SDKs can be categorized according to which two criteria?
options: Game-engine market share and HMD popularity.
Operating system and application-software layer.
Application type and availability.
Hardware layer and rendering method.
questions.explanation: Native deployment SDKs can be categorized by application type, as VR or AR applications, and by availability, as proprietary or open source.

questions.question: Which native VR SDK is associated with the Samsung Gear VR?
options: PSVR SDK
OpenVR SDK
Google VR SDK
Oculus Mobile SDK
questions.explanation: The Samsung Gear VR uses the Oculus Mobile SDK.

questions.question: What is the main function of cloud hosting and rendering support tools for web deployment?
options: They compile and package native mobile applications.
They provide hosting and rendering over a network.
They create 3D models locally on the user's device.
They supply hardware-specific SDKs for head-mounted displays.
questions.explanation: Cloud hosting and rendering support tools only provide hosting and rendering over a network.

questions.question: WebXR, Three.js, AFrame, and Babylon.js are examples of which kind of web deployment tool?
options: Cloud hosting and rendering over a network tools.
Native software development kits for specific VR platforms.
Complete development and deployment tools for applications on the web.
Libraries for development support for deployment over the web.
questions.explanation: WebXR, Three.js, AFrame, and Babylon.js are listed as popular libraries for development support for deployment over the web.

questions.question: ZappAir, 8thWall, InstaVR, and Amazon Sumerian are examples of which category of web deployment tools?
options: Cloud hosting and rendering over a network tools.
Generic development editors for writing code for web-based deployment.
Libraries for development support for deployment over the web.
Complete development and deployment tools for applications on the web.
questions.explanation: These are listed as complete development and deployment tools for applications on the web.

questions.question: What role does Three.js play with WebGL in web-based development?
options: It replaces WebGL with a Vulkan rendering pipeline.
It makes WebGL easier to use and is used for rendering.
It provides a hardware-specific SDK for head-mounted displays.
It hosts the finished experience on a cloud server.
questions.explanation: Three.js makes WebGL easier and is used for rendering.

questions.question: Why can building a virtual world generator from a basic software development kit give a developer more control over performance than using a ready-made generator, while also creating a larger implementation burden?
questions.reference_answer: A ready-made virtual world generator or engine comes with physics and collision support and its own algorithm implementations, which reduces effort but restricts the developer. A basic SDK typically provides drivers, tracking-data access, and calls to graphical rendering libraries, but it does not typically cover every aspect of locomotion, matched motion, physics, or collaborative virtual reality. Therefore the developer must build physics-related support such as avatar movement, collision detection and response, lighting models, and audio support from scratch, can choose and implement physics algorithms according to performance, but must understand and implement the overall system, which is a difficult burden.

questions.question: In a networked collaborative virtual reality experience, why must the virtual reality system still manage virtual collisions even when users are in separate real-world matched zones, and what should collision support include?
questions.reference_answer: Each user has a distinct matched zone, and unwanted physical collision must be avoided when users are close, while users spread around the globe have no possibility of physical collision. Within the shared virtual world, however, user interactions, including collisions, must be managed by the virtual reality system whether users are close or spread around the world. Collision support should therefore include collision detection, which determines whether bodies intersect, and collision response, which determines how they should behave after a collision occurs.

questions.question: Why are a game engine's rendering engine and audio engine associated with different kinds of hardware even though they can be components of the same engine?
questions.reference_answer: A game engine can be thought of schematically as comprising components such as a rendering engine and an audio engine. The rendering engine helps generate animated three-dimensional graphics by methods such as rasterization or ray tracing and is typically built on rendering APIs that provide software abstractions of a graphics processing unit, which is the hardware used for speeding up rendering. The audio engine uses algorithms for loading, modifying, and generating sound, and it can perform its calculations on a central processing unit or on a dedicated application-specific integrated circuit, so it does not require a graphics processing unit.

questions.question: How does native deployment of a virtual reality application depend on a platform-specific software development kit, and how does web deployment change the deployment options available to a developer?
questions.reference_answer: Native application deployment requires SDKs tailored to the platform and hardware, and a platform typically means the operating system plus the hardware. An SDK is a collection of software development tools in one installable package specific to a hardware and operating-system combination, providing fundamental tools to design, build, and test virtual reality experiences. Web application deployment allows the experience to be obtained remotely without a specific device and can use web deployment tools such as cloud hosting and rendering tools, libraries for development support, complete development and deployment tools, generic development editors, or SDK support.
